title: Faith is the gospel condition for being held just—then: does faith alone justify?
source_text: XXV. Nihil ergo probabilius, simplicius, Scripturae magis congruum dici potest, quam justificationem ideo fidei tribui, quia fides conditio est quam Evangelium a nobis exigit, ut apud Deum justi & insontes habeamur, ac sicut cum talibus nobiscum agat Deus, nos propter Christum a poenis peccato debitis eximens, & regni coelestis haeredes instituens. Sed venit hic alia quaestio discutenda, nempe, An fides sola justificet? Solam justificare communis & recepta est Protestantium doctrina; quae tamen cum cautione tradenda & exponenda est, ne quis sit errori & calumniae locus.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing more probable, simpler, or more congruent with Scripture can be said than that justification is attributed to faith because faith is the condition the Gospel requires of us so that we may be held just and innocent before God, and so that God may deal with us as with such—freeing us for Christ's sake from the penalties due for sin and making us heirs of the heavenly kingdom. But here another question comes to be discussed: namely, Does faith alone justify? That faith alone justifies is the common and received doctrine of Protestants; which nevertheless must be handed down and explained with caution, lest there be room for error and calumny.
pass_b_english: Best: faith is the gospel condition under which God holds us just in Christ.
Next question: sola fide—Protestant consensus, but teach it carefully against abuse.
